- Kenya has confirmed its first Ebola case and death. A Kenyan citizen, ill for a month, had traveled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to Kampala, Uganda by road, then flew to Nairobi. He arrived on Saturday, was hospitalized promptly, and died two days later. Authorities believe he may have taken medication to mask symptoms at airport screening. Uganda, Kenya’s neighbor, has reported 20 Ebola cases and two deaths—almost all among people with exposure to the DRC—but Uganda was declared Ebola-free in August. The Kenyan case represents an imported, fatal Ebola infection linked to travel from the DRC with cross-border movement by land and air.
- Imported Bundibugyo-strain Ebola case reaches Kenya after a Kenyan man, treated in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, died in Nairobi. He boarded a flight on Saturday, was screened at the airport, and died on Monday after isolation and a positive test for Ebola. The patient had fallen ill about a month earlier in the DRC and had received care at several hospitals before traveling via Kampala, Uganda, to Nairobi. In the DRC, the latest Bundibugyo outbreak has surpassed 8,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths, yielding a fatality rate of about 48.4%. Vaccines are being trialed but no approved treatment exists. - Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has left nearly 2,000 children orphaned or separated from caregivers since May, when the outbreak was declared. UNICEF reports that more than 1,900 children in eastern DRC have lost or been separated from one or both parents or guardians. The virus kills roughly one in three infected children. Officials caution that actual numbers are likely higher. The report underscores the severe humanitarian toll on families amid ongoing transmission in the region, with no additional laboratory-confirmed case counts or exposure sources detailed. This highlights the broader child protection and public health needs in the outbreak response.
- Kenya confirms its first Ebola case after a citizen returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo died in Nairobi, extending a regional outbreak that has killed more than 4,000. The patient, who had lived in DR Congo for seven years, fell ill about a month ago, traveled by road to Kampala, Uganda, then boarded a Jambojet flight to Nairobi on October 3. He was screened at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport and immediately isolated at Nairobi Hospital; two laboratories confirmed the Bundibugyo strain. He died on Monday night. Authorities have identified 28 contacts and are tracing another 23 passengers and 4 crew members from the same flight. A Kenyan man who had lived in the DRC for seven years fell ill about a month before returning to Nairobi and died shortly after arrival.
